results.title: YouTube Unveils Features That Could Boost Creators but Come With Risks - Business Insider
results.content:
YouTube just announced a flurry of new AI-powered features for creators. But as the platform leans deeper into AI, could it impact perceptions of their authenticity and the originality of their work?

On Wednesday, at the company's annual Made on YouTube event, the platform announced several new features that use generative AI.

The company is revamping its Inspiration Tab in YouTube Studio, adding a new brainstorming tool to help curate video ideas, titles, thumbnails, and outlines. The feature can generate ideas based on a creator's content catalog, comments on their YouTube videos, or videos made by other creators.

Creator startup Spotter recently launched a similar tool for AI-generated video ideas.

results.title: YouTube announces AI features from Google DeepMind for Shorts creators
results.content:
The Veo AI backgrounds are an upgrade over a similar AI-generation feature announced by YouTube in 2023 called Dream Screen. The company said its Veo AI background feature will roll out later this year, while the six-second AI clips will become available in 2025.

Other announcements at the event included new features in the YouTube Studio app that will allow creators to use AI to generate titles, thumbnails and video ideas. Those features will roll out in late 2024, YouTube said.

Creators have been exploring various ways to leverage generative AI technology. Creators have used the new technology to insert clips in their videos or produce entirely AI-generated videos.

However, some creators expressed concerns that their videos on YouTube are used to train the AI models that built Veo.

### 9. Match titles to thumbnails

When creating YouTube titles, it’s important to consider how they pair with thumbnails. The headline should build upon what the preview image shows. This ensures that viewers understand your video and encourages them to click play.

### 10. Use hashtags

Hashtags work best in YouTube Shorts titles, as they help viewers discover your content and related videos on the same topic. Use popular hashtags that are relevant to your video’s subject, and check out what other creators in your niche are including in their titles and thumbnails. [...] ### 7. Avoid clickbait

While certain language can help create mystery and curiosity, avoid using clickbait titles that make exaggerated claims or promise things that the content doesn’t deliver. This will lead to disappointment, frustration and give your YouTube channel a bad reputation. Examples of clickbait titles include phrases like “You won’t believe what happened next…” or “This simple trick will change your life…”

### 8. Ask questions

Questions in titles are a great way to draw attention and encourage clicks. Try to think of questions that your audience would be interested in learning the answers to, such as “How Can You Grow Your YouTube Channel?” or “What Is SEO and Why Should You Care?”

### 9. Match titles to thumbnails [...] Hashtags can be added by typing the # symbol in your title or description, then start typing the best terms for your topic. YouTube will suggest some popular hashtags, and you can choose the best ones for your video. Learn more about hashtag best practices for every social media channel on the Hootsuite blog.

### 11. Follow YouTube's guidelines

YouTube prohibits the use of hate speech, profanity, and harmful content. When creating YouTube titles and thumbnails, be mindful that your content follows YouTube’s community guidelines.
